summary_paragraph: A 70-year-old woman with a history of recurrent lower extremity erythema due to lipodermatosclerosis and chronic venous insufficiency was admitted for bilateral leg redness and swelling that recurred after starting suppressive minocycline. She was afebrile without leukocytosis or other signs of infection. IV antibiotics were initially started but discontinued after infectious disease and dermatology evaluation confirmed an inflammatory rather than infectious etiology. She was treated with a seven-day course of topical clobetasol with plastic wrap and miconazole cream for the toes. Her chronic conditions, including diastolic heart failure, paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, and chronic pancreatitis, remained stable on home medications. She improved clinically and was discharged home with dermatology follow-up planned.
problems: Varicose veins of unspecified lower extremity with inflammation
